chapter: Early listening, piano and adolescent conflict
title: People always said he sounded good
summary: Compliments from age twelve kept him playing, though he did not realize how good he was until recently.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: So we'll just go to this where I say -- I'm talking about when I say that how good you sound, and you say that people always did tell you how good you sound. Go from there.

Well, that's a compliment, and as I was telling you before we turned the tape on, we were discussing this point of music sounding good. And you said that you'd like to hear me play. What I was saying was, which is significant in this period of my life, starting from 12 years old, it seems as though as long as I can remember, people have always told me how good I sound, you know. And as I said, this has naturally been inspirational to me but it has never dawned on me as being a fact, because of my lack of knowledge and desire to study to better myself. And realizing that those who are much better than me.

So I never really realized how good I was, or what I was doing until recently. Now, I would say this, in other words to try to clarify this, I still don't feel I'm good enough, or there's much I want to learn. But I now seem to

realize that there is something in my plan that is original, that is pleasant, that's all the things that I tried to be and tried to say musically. And it now has dawned on me -- and now that it has dawned on me, I am even more determined to try to improve that sound. And I still don't feel I'm as good as I would like to be. But it has been complimentary -- it has been these compliments that started me to playing music at the age of 12, and it has been that that has kept me playing music. It's the fact that someone like you and others has told me that I sound good.

Now, getting back to what we were talking about, in this conversation, if I were to explain why I sound good or anyone sounds good, I would have to say that it is the expression that comes from within you that makes you want to sound good or bad. You see?

So subconsciously there was something that was happening in my life at an early age that made me want to sound good,musically, because it was something I wanted to say verbally that I couldn't say verbally that I could say musically. And it made me feel inspired to have many people come up and pat me on the back and say hey, that sounds good, and later on they started to paying me, which proved to me that it must be better than average.

But thank God for the humility that my father gave me, and my better knowledge and my ability to appraise my own talent as well as others. I know that I'm not as equipped as I should be and I didn't start out as equipped, but I think also this is a challenge that has kept me interested, more interested in music than the other things that I've done. And I'm proud to realize that it can make you happy, make you enjoy what I'm doing.
Yes, yes, you should be proud.
And I'd like to hear more from you about that.
